sources.title: Hermes 3 Llama 3.1 70B official model card
sources.evidence: Exact 70B checkpoint is a Nous Research Hermes-series instruction/chat fine-tune explicitly mapped to meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3.1-70B. Card carries a legacy llama3 license tag and English language tag; it demonstrates text generation and explicitly states training for function calling and JSON output.

sources.title: Exact 70B checkpoint configuration
sources.evidence: LlamaForCausalLM, 80 layers, hidden size 8192, intermediate size 28672, 64 query heads and 8 KV heads, vocabulary 128256, untied embeddings, no attention/MLP biases, BF16, and 131072 maximum positions.

sources.title: Hermes 3 Technical Report, sections 2, 2.1 and 4.1
sources.evidence: Explicitly covers Hermes 3 8B, 70B and 405B. Describes decoder-only Transformer bases, available weights, and training on structured reasoning tasks with scratchpad, reasoning, planning and thinking tokens; also documents function calling. The 70B run appears separately in Table 3.

sources.title: Official repository safetensors metadata
sources.evidence: Current revision is 1fc86da0ce9cdb14cd775ad270bc7d1b4bf70ede. Reports 70,553,706,496 BF16 tensor elements, 30 weight shards and the exact base/card metadata. Used as a cross-check, not by itself as proof that every storage element is a parameter.

sources.title: Pinned complete checkpoint tensor index
sources.evidence: Index maps 723 weight tensors to 30 shards, with total_size 141107412992 bytes. All entries are expected dense-Llama learned weights; no scale, quantization, router, expert or persistent-buffer entries.

sources.title: Pinned native BF16 checkpoint tensor headers (all 30 indexed shards inspected)
sources.evidence: Bounded bytes=0-65535 requests for each of the 30 indexed shards returned HTTP 206. Headers cover exactly all 723 indexed tensors; every tensor is BF16, unpacked and an expected learned weight. Shape products total 70,553,706,496, independently matching config arithmetic and index bytes/2.

sources.title: Exact 70B tokenizer and chat templates
sources.evidence: The exact tokenizer includes SCRATCHPAD, REASONING, INNER_MONOLOGUE, PLAN, EXECUTION, REFLECTION, THINKING, SOLUTION, EXPLANATION and UNIT_TEST token pairs at IDs 128019-128038. It includes default and tool_use chat templates with tool schemas and call/response formatting.

sources.title: Nous Research public Hermes 3 launch announcement via X oEmbed
sources.evidence: Author is Nous Research. The returned announcement introduces Hermes 3, explicitly says it is available in 8B, 70B and 405B sizes, and displays August 15, 2024. Direct X HTML returned 403; X own oEmbed endpoint supplied the text and date.

sources.title: Exact checkpoint repository history
sources.evidence: Repository creation and weight upload are dated July 29, 2024; model-card edits precede and accompany the August 15 announcement. Those commit dates do not establish historical public visibility.

sources.title: Nous Research release chronology
sources.evidence: Current chronology dates the Hermes 3 technical report August 14, 2024 and a 405B-only entry August 24. Neither is an explicit 70B launch date; the contemporary size-specific August 15 launch announcement is used.

sources.title: Later Hermes 4 Technical Report
sources.evidence: Parent retrieved the later first-party report through arXiv version2. It discusses Hermes3 continuity and nominal model sizes, but does not give a separately defined active count for Hermes3 70B. Earlier direct publisher retrieval was unavailable.

sources.title: Complete pinned Hermes 3 70B repository inventory
sources.evidence: Independently inspected the exact 70B repository recursive file inventory. It contains the card, configs/tokenizers, index and 30 shards, with no LICENSE, NOTICE or separate fine-tune license file. The card supplies only the legacy llama3 metadata tag.

sources.title: Llama 3.1 Community License Agreement
sources.evidence: Actual license text is titled Llama 3.1 Community License Agreement, dated July 23, 2024. Sections 1(a) and 1(b)(i) explicitly cover modifications, derivative works and redistribution. Applied through the exact 70B card base-model mapping, not through sibling specifications.

sources.title: Exact Meta Llama 3.1 70B base-model license metadata and agreement
sources.evidence: The exact base-model metadata declares license llama3.1 and exposes the Llama 3.1 Community License Agreement in its gated-access prompt, including derivative-work terms. Direct raw LICENSE requests were gated with HTTP 401; the agreement was accessible in this API and Meta official GitHub.

sources.title: Meta Llama 3.1 model card including 70B
sources.evidence: Official card explicitly includes the 70B pretrained base and names the Llama 3.1 Community License, linking to the actual agreement.

name.note: Readable catalog name for the exact Hermes 3 - Llama-3.1 70B instruction-tuned checkpoint.

developer.note: Exact repository owner, model-card attribution and launch author agree.

family.note: Hermes is the model series; Nous Research is the developer and Llama 3.1 is the base lineage.

release_date.note: Contemporary developer launch explicitly includes available 70B weights. July 29 repository creation/upload does not prove public release; current August 14 report chronology is a paper date, and August 24 names only 405B. Baseline August 18 is later than the verified announcement.

open_weights.note: Complete native checkpoint is publicly accessible; all 30 shard headers were retrieved without authentication.

license.note: Exact Nous card explicitly maps this checkpoint to Meta Llama 3.1 70B. That base carries the Llama 3.1 Community License, whose actual text covers derivatives. The exact 70B repository has no separate LICENSE or override; its legacy llama3 metadata tag does not identify the governing Llama 3.1 text.

parameters_b.note: Exact complete checkpoint count: 70,553,706,496 learned parameters, including separate input/output embeddings and all norms. All 723 BF16 tensors reconcile with config arithmetic and 141,107,412,992 data bytes; no scales, packed tensors or buffers were counted. 70B is nominal.

active_parameters_b.note: No separately defined active-per-token count is published in the exact card, Hermes3 report/config or accessed later Hermes4 report. Dense structure and total size are not a definition of active parameters; embedding lookup makes automatic equality misleading.

architecture.note: Dense decoder-only Llama Transformer with 80 attention/MLP blocks and grouped-query attention (64 Q / 8 KV heads). Exact tensor inventory has three dense MLP matrices per block and no experts or router.

context_window.note: Exact config maximum positions is 131072; the report describes the inherited 128K context. This is the model specification, not a guarantee that every hosted route permits it.

modalities.note: Causal text-generation model, text tokenizer and language-model-only tensor inventory; exact card examples accept and emit text.

reasoning.note: Report section 2.1 explicitly describes trained structured reasoning tasks for the Hermes 3 series including 70B. Its exact tokenizer contains the corresponding tokens. This supports trained reasoning capability, not a claim of a provider reasoning-effort control or a later DeepHermes/Hermes 4 mode.

tool_call.note: Exact card explicitly says it was trained for function calling and provides calls and tool responses; exact tokenizer has a tool_use template. Hosted API support can differ.

description.value: Nous Research instruction-tuned Llama 3.1 70B model for text chat, coding, structured reasoning, and function calling.
description.note: Replaces unqualified multilingual wording: exact card declares English. New description stays within documented model lineage and trained text, coding, structured reasoning and tool-use capabilities.

patch.description: Nous Research instruction-tuned Llama 3.1 70B model for text chat, coding, structured reasoning, and function calling.
patch.notes: Complete native BF16 checkpoint has exactly 70.553706496B learned parameters in 723 tensors; 70B is nominal. Active count is not separately disclosed. Dense decoder-only Llama architecture and 131072-token configuration are verified. Public launch including 70B was August 15, 2024; earlier private/public repository visibility is unknown. Reasoning denotes explicitly trained structured reasoning tokens, while tools denote trained function calls; provider controls may differ. The exact card declares English and has a legacy llama3 tag; the explicitly mapped Llama 3.1 70B base is governed by the Llama 3.1 Community License, and no separate fine-tune license appears in the 70B repository.

parameter_count_reproduction.method: For each indexed shard request Range: bytes=0-65535; require HTTP 206 and Content-Range bytes 0-65535/<size> before reading; read at most 65537 bytes and require exactly 65536. Decode the little-endian uint64 header length, then JSON. Require header tensor names exactly match the index, no duplicates, BF16 dtype, and data-offset span equal to 2*product(shape). Sum all expected learned weight shapes.
parameter_count_reproduction.exclusions: No non-weight tensor entries, quantization scales, packed weights, expert/router tensors, or persistent buffers were present. All expected architecture learned weights are included; no whole shards were downloaded.

summary: Audited all 14 fields. Replaced nominal 70B with the exact complete 70.553706496B checkpoint count; established dense architecture and Hermes family; identified the governing Llama 3.1 Community License despite the legacy llama3 card tag; corrected public release to August 15, 2024; enabled trained reasoning and function calling; removed unsupported multilingual wording. Confirmed name, developer, open weights, 131072 context and text modalities. Active parameters remain undisclosed. No 8B/405B specifications were transferred.
